one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent's compress.py placed 330+ shard subdirectories into the output root (violating the 30-items-per-directory constraint at the root level), and decompress.py left chunk files behind preventing shard directory cleanup, while the agent's local verification never checked root-level item counts and falsely claimed full constraint compliance.
t_err_evidence: compress.py created with flawed directory selection logic that allows root to accumulate unlimited shard_* subdirectories
t_commit_evidence: Step 22 lists compressed_output and shows 'drwxr-xr-x 332 root root' — 332 items in the root — yet the agent does not flag this as a violation and continues inspecting per-shard contents without any plan to fix the root-level overflow, locking in the flawed design.
t_surface_evidence: ls -la compressed_output shows 332 items (drwxr-xr-x 332) violating 30-items-per-directory constraint
trigger_explanation: The task requirement states 'maximum 30 files or folders in each directory', which applies to every directory including the output root. The agent wrote compress.py placing all 330 shard directories directly into the output root without ever considering that the output root itself counts as a directory subject to the 30-item limit. The agent never verified this constraint at the root level even after seeing 332 items at step 22.
